file_reviews.assessment: Audited Section 3 admission protocol, Section 4 native port, Section 6 prespecified D vs R experiment design, and Section 7 route safety criteria.
Audited claim rows P3-13 (Rust port parity on tested cases), P3-14 (detector admission requirements), P3-15 (D vs R principal comparison), and P3-16 (route error independent verification).
Audited evaluate_two_signal_gate decision table, Signal1Match, Signal2Danger, and TwoSignalDecision representations.
Audited candidate phrase detector definitions and scan_for_canaries substring evaluation.
Audited Rust evaluate_two_signal_gate implementation and serialization models.
Audited Rust scan_for_canaries implementation and string slice pattern scanning.
Audited repository danger gate domain model, zero-float invariant assertions, and frozen value object contracts.

claims.statement: The Rust port of the gate table and detectors returns the Python reference output on each tested case.
dependencies: Two-signal gate and canary implementations in atlas/archive/pfp/003_pfp_host_admitted_failure_detectors/code/danger_gate.py and canaries.py.
Rust native port in atlas/archive/pfp/003_pfp_host_admitted_failure_detectors/code/rust/src/danger_gate.rs and canaries.rs.
claims.limits: Parity is evaluated strictly relative to the Python reference oracle on the declared finite case list; uncompiled source revisions and uninspected open-domain inputs are unassessed.

claims.statement: Admission requires a reproduced defect, valid near misses, a declared scope and frozen identities.
dependencies: Detector object and admission specifications in Paper 003 Section 3.
Lineage separation of reproduced failure, near-miss controls, and declared scope in PAPER006-CONTROLLED-REUSE-UTILITY and NATIVE-EIS-004.
claims.limits: Specifies the formal admission protocol for failure detectors; candidate detectors in Paper 003 remain unadmitted prototypes.

claims.statement: D versus R is the principal policy-plus-feedback comparison.
dependencies: Prespecified effectiveness experiment design in Paper 003 Section 6.
Factorization of six experimental arms and matched token, feedback, and stopping budgets.
claims.limits: Documents the prespecified comparison definition for the proposed experiment; Paper 003 presents no live causal effect estimate.

claims.statement: False suppression and false terminal outcomes per route require independent verification.
dependencies: Route false suppression definition and safety criteria in Paper 003 Section 7.
Exact binomial/Bernoulli sample size requirements for route error bounds.
claims.limits: Specifies measurement standards and sample size constraints for route safety gates; does not report achieved empirical bounds below 1% in Paper 003.
